title: Cavatelli al Sugo di Salsiccia Molisano
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Small hand-shaped pasta shells from Molise tossed in a rustic sausage and tomato ragù, a simple, satisfying dish typical of the region's home cooking.
longDesc: Molise's version of cavatelli with sausage ragù leans on generous fennel-forward sausage and a slow-simmered tomato base, a straightforward but deeply satisfying dish found in home kitchens throughout the region.
ingredients: 180 ml (¾ cup) warm water, plus more as needed
400 g (14 oz) Italian sausage, casings removed and crumbled
100 ml (scant ½ cup) dry red wine
60 ml (¼ cup) extra virgin olive oil
Salt and chili flakes, to taste
steps: Mix the semolina, water, and salt into a firm dough, kneading for 10 minutes. Rest, covered, for 20 minutes.
Pinch off small pieces of dough and drag each across a work surface with a fingertip to curl into small shells, setting aside on a floured tray.
Warm the olive oil in a pan and cook the crumbled sausage until browned, breaking it into small pieces.
Add the onion and garlic and sauté until softened.
Add the wine and let it reduce, then add the crushed tomatoes and chili flakes.
Simmer gently for 25–30 minutes until thick and well combined.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the cavatelli until they float and are tender, about 4–5 minutes.
Drain the pasta, reserving some cooking water, and toss into the sauce with a splash of the water.
Finish with fresh basil and serve with grated pecorino.
chefTips: Break the sausage into small, even crumbles for a consistent sauce texture.
The dough should be firm — knead persistently until it comes together properly.
This sauce benefits from a slow simmer, letting the sausage flavor fully infuse the tomato base.
commonMistakes: Rushing the sauce, which needs time to develop real depth from the sausage.
Making the dough too soft, leading to cavatelli that lose their shape when boiled.
Using bland sausage, which is the main flavor driver of this simple dish.
storage: The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days.
reheating: Reheat the sauce gently on the stovetop; cook fresh pasta just before serving.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the sausage and pecorino.
culturalNote: This dish reflects Molise's straightforward, hearty home cooking, a lesser-known Italian region whose cuisine remains deeply tied to family recipes rather than restaurant traditions.
